Avery: Quick question — we're about to flip the 'rapid-rollout' flag for the model-routing canary in prod for 4 orgs. If the canary starts spiking 5xx/latency, who is authorized to flip the kill-switch? Need the short list and any delegation path.
Samir: Short answer: oncall lead or SRE duty only. Longer: policy requires either the primary oncall (pager owner) OR an eng-platform lead + SRE on-call to flip. No ICs alone unless explicitly delegated for that window.
Priya: Is there a documented temporary delegation flow if the oncall person is unreachable for >10m? We might need to hand to Mark (EM) for the 30m maintenance window.
Samir: Delegation exists but must be explicit in the runbook: create an incident ticket, DM @oncall_lead + @sre, and post the delegation line in the ticket body. The 'delegate-kill' form in the runbooks repo records who gets authority and TTL. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kill-switch
Mark: I can take delegation for the 30m window. I'll be on call by phone at +1-555-0102. If anyone tries to flip without the ticket entry, do NOT accept it.
Avery: Thanks — what's the exact command/process to toggle so we can rehearse? Also: what gets captured in audit logs?
Samir: Use the feature-toggle service API or UI. Example CLI (audit automatically appended):

``
ftoggle toggle --flag rapid-rollout --env prod --action off \
  --initiator "Avery" --reason "observed 5xx spike" 
```

The service writes an immutable audit event to /audit/flags and emits to the incident ticket. It also posts to #incidents via the incident bot. The toggle service enforces MFA for prod flips (Token from Vault OTP) and requires an approver header for delegated flips.
Priya: Also confirm: is there an auto-reenable TTL? We don't want to leave customers blocked forever.
Samir: Default behavior: when flipped to OFF via the emergency endpoint it stays OFF until manual reenable UNLESS the 'offramp' route was used, then it will auto-reenable after configured TTL (default 30m). We prefer manual reenable for any user-impacting decision. Offramp is only for short mitigation.
InfraBot: Audit event recorded: flag=rapid-rollout action=created_tutorial_entry user=Samir ts=2026-03-18T17:47:22Z reference=INC-2345
Avery: Good. We'll rehearse the dance with Mark now. Priya — can you add the delegation checklist to the repo and add the exact CLI snippet + MFA note?
Priya: On it. I'll add a short template and ping for a quick dry-run before next maintenance.
Samir: One more guardrail: any flip that affects >1% of traffic must notify Legal & Product via the escalation matrix in the runbook. If >5% traffic impacted, use the exec-notify path.
Avery: Understood. I'll update the canary runbook to include the delegation link and the two-person rule. Will run a dry-run tomorrow 9:30am PT.
Mark: I'll be there for the dry-run. If anyone needs to reach me immediate during the window, @Mark (DM) or call.
InfraBot: Reminder: automated revert is disabled for toggles that have manual hold flag. Make sure to include `--auto-reenable true|false` in the CLI.
Avery: Thanks everyone. Closing thread — will post the incident ticket when we start the canary.
